tools.name: directiq_account_overview
tools.description: Summarize the account in one call: total contacts, active/disabled status counts, list count, tag count, and confirmed sender addresses. A good first call in a conversation, and the way to find a valid "from" address for directiq_send_email. Each section that fails to load is returned as { error } w

tools.name: directiq_get_contact
tools.description: Get one contact by numeric ID: email, first and last name, status, created and updated dates, tags, lists, and notes. Use when you already have the ID; to find a contact, page through directiq_list_contacts. Returns an error if no contact has that ID.

tools.name: directiq_list_contacts
tools.description: List contacts one page at a time, oldest first, with each contact's ID, email, name, status, tags, and lists. Returns { pageNumber, totalCount, result, hasNextPage }; request the next pageNumber while hasNextPage is true. Use to browse contacts or find an ID. For just the total, use directiq_contact

tools.name: directiq_contact_count
tools.description: Return the total number of contacts in the account as a single number. Use for a quick count; for counts plus active/disabled status, lists, tags, and senders, use directiq_account_overview.

tools.name: directiq_upsert_contact
tools.description: Add a contact to a list, creating the contact if the email is new or updating its name if it already exists. Optionally applies tags (created if missing). Use this to create contacts; to change other fields on an existing contact, use directiq_update_contact. Returns import counts (inserted, already

tools.name: directiq_update_contact
tools.description: Update fields on an existing contact by ID, such as firstName, lastName, or email. Only the fields you pass change, and they overwrite the current values. To create a contact, use directiq_upsert_contact; to change list or tag membership, use the list and tag tools.

tools.name: directiq_delete_contact
tools.description: Permanently delete a contact by ID, removing it from every list and tag. This cannot be undone. Confirm with the user first; to only take a contact off one list, use directiq_remove_contact_from_list.

tools.name: directiq_list_lists
tools.description: List every contact list in the account with its ID and name. Use to find a list ID before adding contacts, sending campaigns, or calling directiq_get_list.

tools.name: directiq_get_list
tools.description: Get one contact list by ID: name, created and modified dates, and total, active, and disabled contact counts. Use directiq_list_lists to find the ID. Returns an error if no list has that ID.

tools.name: directiq_create_list
tools.description: Create a new, empty contact list and return it with its new ID. Calling it twice creates two lists with the same name, so check directiq_list_lists first. Add contacts afterwards with directiq_upsert_contact or directiq_add_contact_to_list.

tools.name: directiq_rename_list
tools.description: Rename a contact list by ID. Its contacts are unchanged; the previous name is overwritten.

tools.name: directiq_delete_list
tools.description: Permanently delete a contact list by ID. The contacts themselves are kept, but their membership in this list is lost. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user first.

tools.name: directiq_add_contact_to_list
tools.description: Add an existing contact (by contact ID) to a list. Adding a contact that is already on the list has no effect. To add someone by email who may not exist yet, use directiq_upsert_contact.

tools.name: directiq_remove_contact_from_list
tools.description: Remove a contact from one list. The contact stays in the account and on its other lists; to delete the contact entirely, use directiq_delete_contact.

tools.name: directiq_list_segments
tools.description: List saved segments (rule-based groups of contacts) with their IDs and names. Returns an empty array if the account has none. Segments are managed in the DirectIQ dashboard.

tools.name: directiq_list_tags
tools.description: List every tag in the account with its ID and name. Use to check whether a tag exists or to find its ID before renaming or deleting it.

tools.name: directiq_get_tag
tools.description: Get one tag by ID with its name and details. Use directiq_list_tags to find the ID. Returns an error if no tag has that ID.

tools.name: directiq_create_tag
tools.description: Create a new tag and return it with its ID. Check directiq_list_tags first to avoid duplicates. To tag a contact, use directiq_tag_contact, which also creates missing tags.

tools.name: directiq_rename_tag
tools.description: Rename a tag by ID. Contacts keep the tag under its new name; the previous name is overwritten.

tools.name: directiq_delete_tag
tools.description: Permanently delete a tag by ID and remove it from every contact. Contacts are kept. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user first.

tools.name: directiq_tag_contact
tools.description: Apply one or more tags to a contact by contact ID. Tags that do not exist yet are created. Applying a tag the contact already has has no effect.

tools.name: directiq_untag_contact
tools.description: Remove a tag from a contact, identified by the contact email and the tag name. The tag itself and the contact are kept; to delete the tag everywhere, use directiq_delete_tag.

tools.name: directiq_list_campaigns
tools.description: List email campaigns and automation flows with ID, name, type (Regular or Flow), status, subject, sender, target lists, recipient count, and scheduled send time. Returns { campaigns, nextPageToken }; pass nextPageToken back to get the next page (null means no more). Use the IDs with directiq_campaig

tools.name: directiq_get_campaign
tools.description: Get one campaign by ID: name, type, status, subject, sender, target lists and segments, template ID, recipient count, and scheduled send time. For opens, clicks, and other results, use directiq_campaign_stats.

tools.name: directiq_campaign_stats
tools.description: Summarize how a campaign performed: counts of recipients, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, and complaints, plus open, click, bounce, and unsubscribe rates as percentages of recipients. Use directiq_campaign_report to see which contacts did what. A section that fails to load is returned as an er

tools.name: directiq_campaign_report
tools.description: List the contacts behind one campaign result, one page at a time: who received, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, or complained. Returns { totalCount, result }. Optionally filter to one email address, or for clicks, to one link. For totals and rates only, use directiq_campaign_stats.

tools.name: directiq_send_email
tools.description: Send one transactional email (a receipt, confirmation, or one-to-one message) immediately. It is delivered to real recipients and cannot be recalled, and it counts toward the account’s sending plan. The from address must be a confirmed sender on the account (see directiq_account_overview). Not for b

tools.name: directiq_list_endpoints
tools.description: List known DirectIQ API operations (HTTP method, API group, path, summary). Optionally filter by a search term. Call GET operations with directiq_read_request and POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE operations with directiq_write_request.

tools.name: directiq_read_request
tools.description: Issue an authenticated GET request to any DirectIQ endpoint and return the JSON response. Prefer a dedicated directiq_* tool when one exists; use this for read operations without one, found with directiq_list_endpoints (e.g. segments for a contact, email client reports). Full request/response schema

tools.name: directiq_write_request
tools.description: Issue an authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE request to any DirectIQ endpoint. May create, modify, or permanently delete account data, including bulk operations. Prefer a dedicated directiq_* tool when one exists; use this only for operations without one, found with directiq_list_endpoints, an

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: directiq_get_contact, directiq_list_contacts, directiq_upsert_contact, directiq_update_contact, directiq_add_contact_to_list, directiq_list_campaigns, directiq_campaign_report, directiq_list_endpoints, directiq_read_request · Private data: directiq_account_overview, directiq_get_contact, directiq_list_contacts, directiq_contact_count, directiq_upsert_contact, directiq_update_contact, directiq_delete_contact, directiq_list_lists, directiq_get_list, directiq_create_list, directiq_rename_list, directiq_delete_list, directiq_add_contact_to_list, directiq_remove_contact_from_list, directiq_list_segments, directiq_create_tag, directiq_rename_tag, directiq_delete_tag, directiq_tag_contact, directiq_untag_contact, directiq_campaign_stats, directiq_campaign_report, directiq_read_request, directiq_write_request · Public sink: directiq_get_contact, directiq_list_contacts, directiq_upsert_contact, directiq_update_contact, directiq_add_contact_to_list, directiq_untag_contact, directiq_list_campaigns, directiq_get_campaign, directiq_campaign_report, directiq_send_email, directiq_list_endpoints, directiq_read_request, directiq_write_request · Destructive: directiq_update_contact, directiq_delete_contact, directiq_delete_list, directiq_remove_contact_from_list, directiq_delete_tag, directiq_untag_contact, directiq_list_endpoints, directiq_write_request.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
